summary: Modern Standard Arabic commonly uses a zero copula in present-tense nominal/adjectival predication; overt كان and related forms carry tense/aspect distinctions, while existence/presentation uses separate constructions.

semantic_map.SEM.IDENTITY_EQUIVALENCE: present zero copula in ordinary nominal predication; كان-family when overt tense/aspect is required
semantic_map.SEM.CLASSIFICATION_ROLE: present zero copula + class/role nominal predicate
semantic_map.SEM.CHARACTERISTIC_PROPERTY: present zero copula + adjective/property predicate with agreement/definiteness constraints
semantic_map.SEM.CURRENT_STATE: present zero copula or lexical/state construction; كان-family in past/other tensed contexts
semantic_map.SEM.RESULTANT_STATE: result-state adjective/participle with copular or lexical construction according to syntax
semantic_map.SEM.ENTITY_LOCATION: present nominal sentence with locative predicate; overt tense via كان-family as required
semantic_map.SEM.EXISTENCE_PRESENCE: يوجد / هناك and nominal-presentational constructions by register/context
semantic_map.SEM.TIME_DATE_PREDICATION: nominal/time expression often without overt present copula; tensed constructions differ
semantic_map.SEM.ORIGIN_AFFILIATION: من + origin in nominal predication / nationality adjective
semantic_map.SEM.POSSESSION_AS_EXISTENCE: عند/لدى + possessor and NP is an existence/location-like possession strategy
